title: Guest Property and Unassigned-Room Routing
abstract: Administrative procedure for receiving Wrenfield guest property when no licensed hotel or valid room assignment can be identified.
subject: Guest Property and Unassigned-Room Routing

body.text: Municipal partners may encounter room keys, receipts, luggage tags, toiletries, or other property bearing the Wrenfield name. Accept the property under the local agency's ordinary found-property rules, record the recovery location and time, and forward a copy of the inventory to the Office of Records Analysis. Physical transfer to FUID is not required unless requested.

Do not replace an invalid hotel address with the nearest licensed property. Enter the address exactly as printed and note the parcel conflict separately. A room number may be recorded even when the witness cannot identify a floor or when the room number exceeds the apparent height of the building.

body.label: Legacy credential routing
body.text: Archived Wrenfield worksheets use the memorandum author's directory reference and the filing phrase “unassigned room variance.” The phrase applies when a reported room cannot be matched to a licensed property.

Return ordinary personal property to a verified owner after photographing hotel markings. Retain Wrenfield keys, key sleeves, receipts, and switchboard message cards as case material. Do not attempt to test a recovered key in occupied buildings, and do not mail property to an address printed on Wrenfield stationery.

Guests remain entitled to their personal effects even when the lodging record cannot be reconciled. Confusion regarding a hotel address is not grounds to delay medical care, transportation, or contact with family.
